title: Liquid AI's d1-ultra now available on AI Gateway
description: d1-ultra from Liquid AI is now available on AI Gateway. It is a multimodal decision model for classification, routing, and scoring across text and images, including visual defect inspection and checking damage claims against customer photos. Rather than generating text, d1-ultra returns structured answers with probabilities. Ask a Boolean question to get the probability of a yes/no answer, use Choice to select among named categories, or use Score to rate an ordered scale. You can ask multiple questions about the same input in one request and use the probabilities to decide when to automate an action or request human review. d1-ultra is designed for harder real-world decisions, with an emphasis on calibrated probabilities. It supports a 32,768-token context window and is billed on input tokens only, including image input, with no output-token charges. Use liquid/d1-ultra as the model name. The examples below ask the same question through the AI SDK, OpenAI-compatible Decisions API, and TypeSafe-compatible API: See the decision models documentation for question types and additional usage details. Try d1-ultra in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for accessing models and tracking usage and cost. Decision calls appear in logs and count toward budgets alongside other model requests. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key requests. Browse all decision models available on AI Gateway. Read more

title: Muse Spark Open now available on AI Gateway
description: Muse Spark Open from Meta is now available on AI Gateway. The open-weight reasoning model is designed for coding and agentic workflows, including multi-file refactoring, debugging, and understanding large codebases. Muse Spark Open supports text and image input with a 1M-token context window, allowing agents to work with code and screenshots in the same request. It is available with ZDR and no training, without creating separate provider accounts. Use meta/muse-spark-open as the model name across all API formats and coding agents. The model is available across the AI SDK , the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses APIs, the Anthropic-compatible Messages API , and coding agents connected to AI Gateway. To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select meta/muse-spark-open in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Muse Spark Open in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all language models available on AI Gateway. Read more

title: Vercel Connect now supports Secure Compute
description: Vercel Connect now supports Secure Compute , allowing connectors to reach providers with IP allowlists, such as Salesforce and Snowflake. With Secure Compute routing enabled, Connect’s provider requests use the selected network’s dedicated static IP addresses instead of Connect’s shared IPs. Requests to obtain and refresh access tokens follow that route; your app’s direct API routing is unchanged by this setting. Credential management stays the same, so you don’t need to store long-lived provider secrets in your app or build OAuth flows yourself. To enable Secure Compute routing for a supported connector and all projects that use it: Open your connector’s Settings in the Vercel dashboard. Under Secure Compute Routing , choose an existing network. If your provider uses an IP allowlist, add the selected network’s displayed IP addresses to it in the provider’s settings. Save your changes in Connect. Requests for initial connector creation and all provider discovery requests bypass the selected network and connect directly to providers. If the selected network is unavailable, routed requests fail instead of falling back to Connect’s shared IPs. Read the Secure Compute routing documentation for configuration details. Read more

title: Cat Jam is now available in stealth for free on AI Gateway
description: Cat Jam is now available on AI Gateway as a stealth model, free to use during the stealth period. Cat Jam is a reasoning model for coding and agentic tasks, with low-latency inference. It supports function calling , so agents can connect it to your own tools, and structured outputs that follow a JSON schema you supply. Responses include the model's reasoning text alongside the answer. Cat Jam takes text input only. Cat Jam supports low , medium , high , xhigh , and max reasoning efforts. Zero Data Retention (ZDR) is not available for this model. Prompts may be retained for safety reasons. Cat Jam works with the AI SDK , the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses APIs, the Anthropic-compatible Messages API , and coding agents connected to AI Gateway. Use stealth /cat-jam as the model name: To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select stealth/cat-jam in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Cat Jam in the model playground . title: Vercel Drives is now generally available
description: Vercel Drives is now generally available for Vercel Sandbox on Hobby, Pro, and Enterprise. A Drive is persistent storage that you mount as a directory in a Vercel Sandbox. Its files remain available after the sandbox stops, so later runs and other sandboxes can access them by mounting the same Drive. Use Drives to preserve an agent’s workspace or file-based memory across runs, or to make datasets, models, dependencies, and build artifacts available across sandboxes. You can also fork a Drive into independent writable Drives. Forks inherit the source Drive's data, region, and maximum size, then store their own changes. Parallel workers can start with the same files and make changes without affecting the original or one another. Learn more in the Drives documentation . Read more

title: Bring Your Own Cloud on AWS is now generally available
description: Enterprise teams can now run Vercel Functions in their own AWS account with Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC). With BYOC, your function code and execution stay inside your security and compliance boundary. Vercel continues to handle deployments, environments, routing, and static assets. During deployment, you provision functions in your AWS account and Vercel serves everything else. You keep control over function execution with your own IAM permissions, network access, and resource lifecycle policies. With BYOC, you can: Run Node.js and Python Vercel Functions in your AWS account Meet strict compliance, security, and isolation requirements Connect privately to backends and services in your VPC Use existing AWS commitments BYOC is available on Enterprise plans. Contact sales or your account team to get started, or learn more in the documentation , and read the complete guide to BYOC . Read more

title: Vercel Connect adds Enterprise-Managed Authorization
description: Vercel Connect now supports Enterprise-Managed Authorization (EMA) in public beta. Your apps and agents can access supported services on behalf of signed-in users without separate consent prompts for each service. Here's how access works: Admin-managed access: Administrators can grant or revoke access to supported services through the identity provider. Corporate sign-in: Users sign into your app with their corporate account through a compatible identity provider such as Okta . Scoped tokens: Your app requests the scopes it needs, and Connect handles token exchange, caching, and renewal. Access is limited to approved scopes and the user’s existing service permissions. If your app uses Vercel Passport , you can request a token for Slack’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) server with the signed-in user’s identity: type: embedded-entry-inline id: 1T9cFkjaRDDmRFQ5bWVmD6 Connect supports Cross-App Access (XAA) , including its use for MCP authorization through EMA. Follow the Vercel Connect EMA setup guide to configure your identity provider and services and enable EMA on their Connect connectors. Read more

title: MCP Events support in Vercel Connect is now in public beta
description: Vercel Connect now supports MCP Events in public beta, allowing your apps and agents to subscribe to webhook events from compatible MCP servers. Build agents for tasks like summarizing new messages, reviewing newly created issues, or responding to document feedback. Connect creates subscriptions on the MCP server and renews them automatically as needed, verifying the server’s webhooks and forwarding events to your application using authenticated delivery. You can use the Connect SDK to subscribe to MCP events: type: embedded-entry-inline id: 4OcwkT5TX5v1h28r0qLS1C At your delivery endpoint, use the SDK to verify that each delivery came from Connect before acknowledging receipt: type: embedded-entry-inline id: 2B5UlAEUePpGMQg3S2hD1L You can also expose AI SDK event discovery and subscription APIs as agent tools, using Connect’s MCP Events adapter to manage subscriptions. In eve , enabling events on an MCP connection gives agents tools to discover the server’s events and use Connect to create, inspect, or stop subscriptions. Read the MCP Events docs and Vercel Connect quickstart for SDK setup and authentication. Read more
